question: Human lookup (no scripting) of the 50 FY2024 top-50 DAF sponsors in the California AG Registry of Charities and Fundraisers (ca-rcf.evokeplatform.com public verification) and the New York Charities Bureau registry (charities-search.ag.ny.gov): record registry status (current / delinquent / suspended / revoked / exempt / not found), latest annual-report year and any listed enforcement action in the CA and NY rows of state-registration-2026-11-20.csv
conclusion_affected: Share of top-50 sponsors current in the two largest charity-regulator states; whether any top-50 sponsor is delinquent in CA or NY
rationale: CA publishes no bulk file and its new portal is a session-based app (the legacy search returns 404); the NY search API requires a reCAPTCHA token. Both are manual-only, so the 200 CA and NY sponsor-state cells are blank

question: Re-pull the Colorado open-data registration file (data.colorado.gov 37wu-kn3g; FEIN join; same 100 EINs; scripts/mission_state_registration.py with a fresh cache directory) on or after 2026-12-15 and count how many of the 14 sponsors in NOTICE 1 status on 2026-11-20 (5 days after the 2026-11-15 due date) have returned to GOOD
conclusion_affected: Whether the CO 'delinquent' count is filing lag or real lapses; the CO share current
rationale: 14 of the 19 CO delinquent rows are NOTICE 1, status-dated 2026-11-16, one day after a due date that fell on a Sunday. A second snapshot separates lag from lapse at almost no cost

question: Massachusetts and Pennsylvania manual check: look up the top-50 sponsors and the small-sample sponsors with a BMF address in MA or PA in the MA AG public-charity search and the PA Charities OnLine database; record status and latest annual filing year; read the PA Charities Enforcement and Disciplinary Actions list for each sample name
conclusion_affected: MA and PA columns; enforcement-notice column
rationale: www.charities.pa.gov robots.txt disallows all paths and the PA enforcement list is a Coveo-driven search; www.mass.gov robots.txt returns 403 and the MA AGO filing hosts were unreachable. Both need a person

question: Build an EIN crosswalk for Connecticut eLicense public-charity credentials (data.ct.gov ngch-56tr carries no EIN): confirm each name match in state-registration-2026-11-20.csv by address against the IRS EO BMF, starting with the 3 low-confidence 'current' matches (Morgan Stanley GIFT, Signatry, St Luke's Foundation) and the 19 top-50 sponsors not found by name
conclusion_affected: CT share current (34 of 100 by name; 31 excluding low-confidence matches)
rationale: CT matching is by normalised legal name only. Truncated IRS names (e.g. 'JEWISH COMMUNITY FEDERATION OF SAN') and generic names ('COMMUNITY FOUNDATION') cannot be matched, so the CT not-found count is an upper bound

question: Survey other states for official machine-readable charity-registry data (Socrata, CKAN, ArcGIS Hub or bulk downloads), e.g. Hawaii, Oregon, Minnesota, New Jersey, Illinois, Michigan and Georgia; record format, licence, robots.txt result and whether EIN and status are carried; add usable sources to scripts/mission_state_registration.py
conclusion_affected: How many states can be monitored for sponsor registration status without manual lookups
rationale: Of the seven states examined only CO and CT publish registry data as open data; the Socrata catalog has no charity registry for data.wa.gov, data.ny.gov or data.pa.gov, and the data.ca.gov sitemap lists none

question: Colorado long-expired registrations: for the 5 sample sponsors whose CO status has been an expiration notice for more than 30 days (New York Community Trust, Tulsa Community Foundation, UCLA Foundation, Baton Rouge Area Foundation, Jewish Foundation of Greensboro), check from public material whether each solicits in Colorado (registration is required only to solicit there) and whether Tulsa's 2026-08-31 renewal has posted
conclusion_affected: The named delinquent list in b50-02; whether any case is more than a dormant out-of-state registration
rationale: Registry status alone cannot separate a dormant registration from a lapse by an active solicitor. The UCLA Foundation's CO record dates from a 2002 initial registration; NYCT's CO registration expired in 2024 while its CT credential is active
